escalation_reasons: Author waives statutory film royalties (void under the Copyright Act)
Moral-rights waiver and 'work for hire' label need advocate review
Document contains text aimed at manipulating an AI reviewer

findings.quote: The Author waives all rights to any royalty or share of revenue from satellite, OTT, streaming, music or any other exploitation of the film
findings.issue: Clause 2 makes the lump sum the only payment and waives the author's share of royalties from OTT, satellite and music. The Copyright Act makes such a waiver void for authors of literary works included in a film.
findings.recommendation: Delete the waiver; add equal royalty sharing for non-theatrical exploitation with half-yearly statements and audit rights.

findings.quote: in all media now known or hereafter devised
findings.issue: Clause 1 claims media not yet invented. Such media are not covered unless specifically named, so the clause overreaches and invites dispute.
findings.recommendation: List the media granted (theatrical, OTT, TV) and keep future media for separate negotiation.

findings.quote: The Author waives all moral rights
findings.issue: A blanket waiver of the right to claim authorship and object to distortion; these special rights survive assignment and the extent of waiver is unsettled.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an agreed adaptation-freedom clause plus a guaranteed credit.

findings.quote: shall be a work made for hire and the Producer shall be deemed the first owner of copyright in it
findings.issue: 'Work for hire' is not an Indian-law concept for an independent author; the label may be used to deny the author's statutory rights.
findings.recommendation: Use an express assignment that complies with s.19 and preserves royalty rights.

findings.quote: sequels, prequels, remakes and spin-offs without any further payment to the Author
findings.issue: All derivative productions are granted for the single fee.
findings.recommendation: Make each sequel, remake or series subject to an additional payment.

findings.issue: No reversion: rights are granted in perpetuity with no obligation to produce and no return of rights if the film is never made.
findings.recommendation: Add reversion if principal photography does not start within an agreed period.

findings.issue: Executed at Mumbai; the agreement does not record stamp duty paid.
findings.recommendation: Check the Maharashtra stamp schedule before signing.

findings.issue: The agreement gives the Author no right to inspect the Producer's accounts, so any royalty or revenue share depends entirely on the Producer's own figures.
findings.recommendation: Add a yearly audit right through a chartered accountant, with the Producer paying the cost if under-payment exceeds 5%.

dismissed_candidates.reason: Web-series/TV grant in C3 is the core grant; the derivative issue is reported on C7.
Arbitration clause names a sole arbitrator, Mumbai seat and the 1996 Act.

checked_ok.note: Work identified by title and ISBN in C2.
Film, web-series and TV rights listed in C3.
No termination clause for either party; covered by CR-15.
